text:
Elaine_security: Heads-up — we received a user request to export + delete all personal data for user_id=U-9182 in the EU region. They attached a notarized ID PDF but the email domain in the notarized document doesn't match their account email. Legal said they might accept, privacy wants stronger proof. What evidence do we accept and how should we record this in the audit log?

Dsar-bot: Attachment uploaded: user_evidence_U-9182.pdf (sha256: 3a7f...b2c) — automatic checksum recorded.

Samir_privacy: Notarized ID + an email reply from the account is typical. If the domain mismatch is small (old company email) we can accept with secondary proof (last login IP or phone OTP). We also need `evidence_type` and `verifier` fields in the audit log entry, and a `retention_exception` flag when we temporarily keep backups.

Yara_legal: Notarized ID is usually enough, but prefer corroboration: matching email OR phone on record OR last login timestamp within 6 months. If we can't get that, escalate to legal intake. Also capture the legal basis for any retention exception.

Chris_sre: From infra side: deletion runs via our job `delete-job --user-id U-9182 --run-id R-2026-04-02T10` which writes events to `s3://redwood-audit/deletes/`. KMS wraps those objects; note KMS key rotation happens weekly — deletion must record `kms_key_id` used to encrypt backups and snapshots so we can decrypt if needed for forensics. If a key rotates mid-operation we need to pin the key id in the job metadata.

Elaine_security: Proposal: no broad RBAC exceptions. Create a short-lived role `dsar-verifier` with minimal perms: read user metadata, view evidence attachments, and mark `deletion_approved`. Require membership via SSO group + MFA and log every action. Can we implement that without giving support broader delete rights?

Samir_privacy: That works. Also suggest a 2-person approval for high-risk accounts (admins, financial data). For normal consumer accounts, single verifier + evidence_type certified is ok. Add a `requested_evidence` field to the audit payload so we know what we asked for.

Yara_legal: 2-person approval is heavy. Proposed triage: if evidence contains notarized ID AND either phone OR matching last login within 6 months, auto-approve. If evidence is partial, escalate to legal (manual). For retention exceptions: legal can approve a short retention window (e.g., 30 days) but must set `retention_exception:{reason:'legal_review', expires:'ISO-8601-date'}` in the audit record.

Chris_sre: Implementation notes: change delete job to emit a structured line in the immutable audit log, e.g.:
```
DELETE_REQUEST user=U-9182 run=R-2026-04-02T10 evidence=notarized_id verifier=elaine_security outcome=approved retention_exception=none kms_key_id=key-abc123
```
Also persist the original request payload (read-only) to an append-only store so we can replay.

Elaine_security: Q: If legal signs off on a retention exception (keep backups for N days), how do we flag ops so the cleaner doesn't purge those backups? We need TTL + reason surfaced to the retention job.

Yara_legal: Add `retention_exception` as structured metadata: `{"reason":"legal_review","authorized_by":"yara_legal","expires":"2026-05-02T00:00:00Z"}` — and ensure retention job checks that metadata before deleting.

Samir_privacy: Security concern — could someone exploit the verifier flow to delete other users? Require that the `dsar-verifier` role can only approve deletions for requests that match the `requester_email` on the account and that the verifier action requires SSO, MFA, and an approval comment. Add an alert for abnormal activity (e.g., >10 deletions/day by a single verifier).

Chris_sre: Agree. Suggested alert rule: `sum(delete_count) > 10 over 24h AND verifier in group:d sar-verifier` -> page security. Also make the audit log include `verifier_sso_subject` and `verifier_mfa=true`. We should also emit a `vuln_triage_context` tag if deletion is part of an incident-driven cleanup.

Elaine_security: I'll draft the RBAC change + the minimal policy for `dsar-verifier`, plus the alert and the schema changes for audit logs (`evidence_type`, `kms_key_id`, `retention_exception`, `verifier_sso_subject`). Ping @yara_legal and @samir_privacy for signoff on the acceptance criteria. :thumbsup:

Samir_privacy: Sounds good. If you can add the exact log schema and sample payloads I can add to the privacy runbook.

Yara_legal: I'll review the retention exception language. If we need an emergency legal hold we will append `legal_hold:true` and set a longer expiry.

Chris_sre: I'll queue the delete-job change and KMS pinning in the next sprint. Will include unit tests to assert `kms_key_id` present in job metadata.

Elaine_security: Thanks — I'll create the GH PR with the RBAC proposal and link it here when ready.
